transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um, thank you so much for seeing me. I, well... I guess I'm here because I've been having a little trouble with my eating habits? I hope I'm in the right place for this. 

It's just that, um, on these late work nights—I'm a graphic designer, so my deadlines can get kind of crazy—I'll order what I tell myself is just a normal dinner. But then it sort of... turns into a whole entrée, and sides, and dessert, and then I even end up getting extra snacks from my kitchen. It ends up being way, way more than I’d ever eat if someone were actually sitting across from me. 

I feel a little embarrassed even admitting that out loud, to be honest. But... does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing I should be talking about here?
Do you feel guilty after these late-night eating episodes?

Um, guilty? I... I don't know if I'd use that word, exactly. 

I mean, I guess I haven't really noticed feeling a lot of guilt about it? It's more just... realizing I probably shouldn't have eaten quite that much, and feeling a little too full. But I try not to make a big deal out of it, you know? I just sort of tell myself I'll eat a lighter lunch the next day and try to get right back to my design work. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I just haven't really thought about it in terms of feeling guilty, if that makes sense.
Do you ever make yourself vomit or use laxatives after one of these late-night eating episodes?

Oh, my goodness, no. I... I definitely don't do anything like that. 

Um, throwing up or taking laxatives, that sounds really intense, and I don't think I could ever bring myself to do that. I just sort of sit there and wait for the really full feeling to pass, or just go to sleep. I know some people really struggle with those kinds of things, but I promise I don't do anything like that. 

I hope it's okay that my answer is no? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information, and I'd hate for you to think I was doing something dangerous like that.
How often do these late-night eating episodes happen?

Um, how often? Well, I try to keep it under control, I really do. It's not an everyday thing or anything like that. 

But... well, if I'm being completely honest, and I look back at my food delivery receipts and my work calendar, it's usually at least one night every week. Sometimes maybe two, if the deadlines are really piling up. And I guess... I guess it's been happening like that for a few months now? 

I know that probably sounds like a lot, and I'm trying to do better, I promise. Is that... is that a normal amount for someone dealing with work stress? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline.
Do you ever fast or severely restrict your food intake on the days following one of these late-night eating episodes?

Um, no, I definitely don't do that. I know I mentioned earlier that I might have a lighter lunch sometimes, but I don't ever fast or stop eating altogether. 

I try really hard to just get right back to my normal routine the next day. I'll still have my regular meals, just... maybe not quite as heavy if I'm still feeling a little full from the night before. But I definitely don't starve myself or skip meals or do anything extreme. I know that's not healthy, so I make sure to avoid it. 

Is... is that the right way to handle it? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by trying to keep up with my regular eating schedule.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating or control how much you're eating during these late-night episodes?

Um... control... well, I wouldn't say I completely lose my mind or anything like that. I'm still, you know, aware of what's happening. 

But... I guess, if I'm really thinking about it... once I start, there's sort of this point where I'm just watching myself. Like, I'll be clicking back to the food delivery app, or opening another package from the pantry, and in my head, I'm thinking, "I should probably stop now." But... it just feels like the decision has kind of already slipped out of my hands? Like I'm just going along with it, even though I know I shouldn't be. 

I know that sounds really bad, like I have no willpower at all. I really try to be disciplined, I promise. It's just in those specific moments, it gets a little fuzzy. Does that make sense? I hope you don't think I'm completely out of control, because I do try my best most of the time.
Would you say that during these late-night eating episodes, you're eating much more quickly than you normally would?

Um, quickly? Well, I try to chew my food and, you know, enjoy it. I'm not just inhaling it or anything. 

But... I guess when I'm working late, and I have all these Illustrator files open on my screens, I might be eating a little faster than usual. It's just because I'm trying to multitask, you know? But sometimes... sometimes I'll be moving from one container to the next, and before I know it, I've kind of finished most of it in just a few minutes. I barely even notice the taste because I'm so focused on my work. 

I know I should probably slow down and be more mindful, and I'm really going to try to do that. Is it pretty common for people to eat faster when they're working at their desk like that? I just want to make sure I'm not doing something completely abnormal.
Do you usually eat during these late nights because you're feeling stressed or anxious about your work deadlines?

Um, stressed? Well, I mean, everyone gets a little stressed about deadlines, right? It's just part of being a graphic designer. 

But I wouldn't say I'm eating *because* I'm anxious. It's more just... it's just late, and I'm awake, and I need a little energy to keep going. I really try to manage my stress well, you know, with deep breathing and staying organized. I'm definitely not one of those people who just eats their feelings, if that's what you mean. 

I guess sometimes the work just piles up, and having a snack just kind of helps me stay focused at my desk. But it's not like an emotional thing. Is... is it okay that I just get a little hungry when I'm working late like that? I just want to be sure I'm explaining it right.
Do you feel like you're unable to stop eating once you've started during these late-night episodes?

Um... wait, didn't you just ask me that? Or... maybe I misunderstood before. I'm sorry, I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers. 

Like I was trying to say earlier, it's not that I can't stop at all. I can! It's just... well, sometimes it's like I get into this zone with my work and the food is just right there next to my keyboard. I don't feel completely out of control, I promise. It's more like a bad habit of snacking while I'm distracted, you know? 

I really am trying to be better about it. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay this time.
Do you feel like you're eating without thinking about what or how much you're eating during these late-night episodes?

Um, without thinking? Well, I try to be mindful. I really do. I've read all about mindful eating and I know how important it is. 

But I guess... well, sometimes it's like my hands are just moving on their own while I'm looking at my screen. It's not that I'm completely mindless, it's just that... once I start, there's this moment where I can kind of see myself reaching for another package, or clicking back over to where the food is. And in my head, I'm thinking, "Okay, I should probably stop now," but... it's almost like the decision just kind of slips away from me for a minute. 

I know that probably sounds terrible, and I really am working on being more present when I eat. Is it... is it normal to feel a little bit disconnected like that when you're super focused on a project? I just want to make sure I'm not sounding totally crazy.
Do you feel like your eating habits are affecting your daily life or causing you significant distress?

Um, significant distress? I mean... I wouldn't say it's ruining my life or anything dramatic like that. I still get all my work done, and my clients are really happy with my designs. I make sure it doesn't interfere with my actual job. 

I guess... well, I do feel a little bad about it sometimes the next morning. Like, I'll see the wrappers in the trash and feel a bit silly that I let myself snack so much. But it's not like I'm crying over it or anything. It's just a little frustrating because I really want to be healthy, you know? 

I definitely don't want to make it sound like a bigger deal than it is. Everyone has things they want to improve about themselves, right? I'm just trying to figure out how to balance my late-night work with better habits. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for... does that make sense?
Have you had these late-night eating episodes at least once a week for the past three months?

Um, I guess... well, I really didn't think it was that frequent at first. I try to keep a good routine, I really do. But... I actually looked back at my delivery receipts and my work calendar recently, just because I wanted to make sure I was giving you the right information today. 

And, um, I guess there is usually at least one night every week where this happens. Sometimes maybe a little more if I have a big design project due. And... yeah, I suppose that pattern has been going on for several months now. 

But it's mostly just that one night, which isn't too terrible, right? I mean, I hope it doesn't make me sound completely out of control. I'm just trying to be as honest as I can so I can get better. Did I answer that okay?
Do you feel like you're eating more than you intended to during these late-night episodes?

Um, more than I intended? Well... I try to be really careful about what I buy, you know? I usually just get those little snack packs so I don't overdo it. 

I guess... sometimes I might open a second one. Or, well, maybe I end up finishing the whole box of them if I'm up really late working on a design. But it's just because I'm trying to stay awake and focused, not because I'm trying to eat a lot. I really don't mean to eat the whole thing when I start. 

I know I shouldn't do that, and I'm really trying to get better at just having one and stopping. Is it pretty common for people to misjudge how much they're going to eat when they're working late? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of examples.
Do you feel like you're unable to control how much you're eating once you start during these episodes?

Um, unable to control it? I mean, I wouldn't say I'm completely out of control, like I'm in a trance or anything scary like that. I still know what I'm doing. 

But... well, I guess there is this point, once I start, where... I don't know, it's hard to explain without sounding silly. I'll be sitting there, maybe opening another package, and in my head, I'm thinking, "Okay, I should probably stop now, I don't really need this." But my hands are just kind of... already doing it. It feels a little bit like the decision has just slipped away from me for a minute. 

It's not that I *can't* stop, exactly, I just... I get really absorbed in what I'm doing, I guess? I really hope that doesn't make me sound weak or anything. I'm usually very disciplined with my work and my schedule. Is it normal to feel a little bit like that when you're tired and stressed? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it the right way for you.
Do you feel like you're eating more rapidly than usual during these episodes because you feel like you can't stop?

Um, faster than usual? Well... I try to eat mindfully, I really do. I know that's important for digestion and everything. 

But, um... I guess when I'm at my desk and I'm really stressed about a deadline, I do eat a bit... quicker. It's not that I'm trying to gorge myself or anything! It's just... I'll have my Illustrator files open, and I'm trying to get things done, and I just sort of... move from one container to the next. 

Sometimes, I'll look down and realize I've finished most of it in just a few minutes, and I haven't even really tasted it. I think I just get so focused on the screen that I don't realize how quickly I'm eating. It's just a bad habit when I'm working, I think. Does that make sense? I'm trying to be better about stepping away from my desk to eat, I promise.
Do you feel like you're unable to control your eating during these late-night episodes because you're feeling overwhelmed or distracted by your work?

Um, overwhelmed by work? Well... I mean, the work is definitely stressful, and I do get really focused on it. But... I think it's a little more than just being distracted, maybe? 

Like I was trying to say before... it's just this weird feeling. Once I start eating, there's this point where... I'm literally watching myself keep reaching back for the food, or opening another package, and in my head I'm thinking, "Okay, I really should stop now." But it just feels like... like the decision has already slipped out of my hands, somehow. 

I know that sounds terrible, like I have no willpower at all. I really am trying to be more disciplined about it. Is it okay that I'm explaining it this way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what happens, even if it's a little embarrassing to admit.
Do you ever feel guilty or remorseful after one of these late-night eating episodes?

Um, guilty? Well... no, I don't think I'd use a strong word like remorse. I really try my best not to beat myself up over things, you know? I know some people get really upset with themselves, but I just... I try to stay positive. 

I mean, maybe I feel a tiny bit annoyed that I messed up my calorie count for the day, but it's just a little extra food, right? I usually just tidy up my desk, throw the wrappers away, and tell myself I'll just have a lighter breakfast the next morning to balance it out. 

I feel like it's better not to dwell on the negative, so I just kind of move on. That's a pretty healthy way to handle it, don't you think? I really try to keep a good attitude about everything, I hope that's the right approach.
Do you feel like you're unable to control what you're eating during these late-night episodes because you feel like you've lost control over your eating?

Um, lost control? Well... I guess maybe we're kind of circling back to what I was trying to explain a minute ago. I really hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is! 

But yes, um... like I said, once I start eating, there's just this moment where... I'm literally watching myself reach for more food, or, you know, open another package. And in my head, I'm fully aware, thinking, "Okay, I really need to stop now." But it just feels like... like the decision isn't mine anymore? Like it just slipped out of my hands. 

I know that probably sounds like I'm not trying hard enough, and I really don't want you to think I'm just giving up. I am trying to be better about it, I promise. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay... I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right.
Do you feel like you have no control over what you're eating during these late-night episodes?

Um, yeah... I guess we are kind of talking about the same thing again, aren't we? I hope I'm not being confusing. I really want to be helpful here. 

But, um, yes... it's just like I was saying. It's not that I want to lose control, it's just... once I get going, it's like I hit this point where I'm just watching myself. Like I'm seeing my hand go for another snack, or opening something else, and my brain is saying, "You really should put that down now." But... it just feels like the choice isn't mine to make in that moment. Like it's just happening anyway. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound completely out of control or anything. I mean, I do stop eventually! I just... I struggle with that one part of it. Is that... is that the kind of thing you're asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you feel like you have no control over how much you eat during these late-night episodes?

Um, yeah, I... I think we're still on the same track here. I'm so sorry if I'm repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need. 

But yes, regarding how much I eat... it's exactly like I was trying to describe. Once I start, I hit this point where I'm just sort of... watching myself. Like I see myself reaching for more, or opening another package, and I'm thinking to myself, "Okay, I really should stop now." But it just feels like the decision has already slipped out of my hands. 

I really don't want to sound like I'm totally helpless or making excuses. I mean, I do try to keep it reasonable! It's just that specific moment where it feels a bit... automatic? I hope that makes sense. Am I answering your questions okay? I just really want to be helpful.
